title: Forms of Business Organization
tagline: Sole proprietorship, partnership, companies, public-sector undertakings and cooperatives: how each is organised and who each suits. Unit weight: 25 marks.

overview.intro: The form a business takes decides how much capital it can raise, how many owners it can have, how it is taxed, how far the owners are personally liable, and how easily it can be transferred. This is the largest unit in the registered Commerce syllabus at twenty-five of the eighty marks, so it repays a thorough treatment. This unit works through the sole proprietorship, the partnership including the limited liability partnership, the cooperative society, the statutory company, the public-sector undertaking and the private and public limited company, comparing them on the accepted bases of formation, liability, continuity, management and suitability.

facts.label: Ownership forms
facts.value: Sole proprietorship, partnership, cooperative, company, public-sector undertaking.

learningOutcomes: Define and describe the sole proprietorship and its merits and limitations.
Explain partnership, its essentials and the types of partner.
Describe the company form, including private and public limited companies.
Compare all forms on the standard bases of comparison.

blocks.text: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and usually managed by one person who supplies the capital, bears the risk and keeps the profit. It is the simplest and oldest form: registration is not compulsory, decision making rests entirely with the owner, and the law treats the business and the owner as one person. That identity is the source of both its strength and its weakness. Because the owner and the business are the same in law, the owner has unlimited liability, meaning creditors can reach her personal property if the business cannot pay.

blocks.caption: Sole proprietorship: merits and limitations
rows: Unlimited personal liability of the owner
Burden of all skills resting on one person
Uncertainty: the business ends with the owner

blocks.text: Suitability follows from those features. It suits a small retail or service business in a single location where the owner can supervise directly and the capital needed is modest, such as a neighbourhood grocery, a tailoring unit or a repair shop. It is unsuitable where large capital, specialised management or perpetual succession matter.

items.text: A repair technician who buys tools and fixes appliances from a rented room.
items.note: Low capital, one skill, local customers: the form fits the activity exactly.

items.text: A chain of supermarkets needing capital from hundreds of investors.
items.note: Sole proprietorship cannot raise that capital, which is why the company form is used instead.

learn.title: Partnership and the limited liability partnership

blocks.text: Partnership is the relation between persons who agree to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. Its essentials are a voluntary agreement, at least two persons, a lawful business, sharing of profits, and mutual agency, which means that each partner can bind the firm through acts done in the ordinary course of business. Partnerships are governed by the Indian Partnership Act, and although registration is not compulsory, an unregistered partnership cannot sue its own partners or third parties to enforce a contract.

blocks.caption: Types of partner and what each contributes
rows: Manages day to day and takes part in decision making
Contributes capital but does not participate in management
Lends the use of a name or reputation without capital or profit share
Exists as a partner but is not known to the public
Entitled to share profits but not liable for losses personally

blocks.text: The limited liability partnership was created to answer the partnership’s greatest weakness: under ordinary partnership every partner is jointly and severally liable without limit, so one partner’s negligence could consume another’s house. In a limited liability partnership at least two designated partners hold unlimited liability while the liability of every other partner is limited to their contribution, and the structure protects a partner from the acts of another partner committed without authority.

items: Merits: more capital than a sole proprietorship, shared skill, better decision through discussion, simple formation.
Limitations: unlimited liability in an ordinary partnership, difficulty of transferring interest, no perpetual succession, disputes between partners.
Suitability: professional firms, trading businesses of moderate size, and ventures needing two or more complementary skills.

items.text: Three architects pooling capital and clients to open a practice.
items.note: Shared skill and capital make partnership appropriate, while unlimited liability argues for the limited liability partnership form.

items.text: A silent partner who invests but never appears in the firm’s dealings.
items.note: Liability and management are both limited by the role, though the liability remains unlimited in an ordinary partnership.

learn.title: The company form: private and public limited companies

blocks.text: A company is an artificial person created by law, separate from its members, with perpetual succession, a common seal, the power to hold property, sue and be sued, and limited liability for its shareholders. It is incorporated under the Companies Act, and its ownership is divided into shares that can be transferred subject to the articles. A private limited company restricts the transfer of shares, forbids public invitation for share capital and limits its membership, while a public limited company may invite the public to subscribe and can be listed on a stock exchange, subject to stricter disclosure.

blocks.caption: Private limited against public limited company

blocks.text: The merits of the company form are limited liability, large-scale capital raising, professional management, perpetual succession and easy transfer of interest. The demerits are costly formation and compliance, formal regulation by the registrars, divided ownership which can weaken the interest of individual shareholders, and the possibility that managers run the company for themselves rather than for the owners.

A cooperative society is a voluntary association of persons of modest means who join together for a common economic purpose on the democratic principle of one member one vote. It is incorporated separately, has limited liability for its members, and enjoys tax concessions. Common types are consumer cooperatives which buy in bulk and sell at fair prices, producer cooperatives which combine small producers, credit cooperatives which lend at reasonable rates, and marketing cooperatives which sell members’ output collectively.

A public-sector undertaking is a business owned and controlled wholly or partly by the government, established to serve public interest rather than private gain. Its merits are access to huge public capital, service in areas private firms find unprofitable, employment generation and operations in strategic sectors. Its limitations are bureaucratic decision making, political interference in appointments and pricing, and accountability that runs to the legislature rather than to shareholders.

blocks.caption: Cooperative against public-sector undertaking
rows: The government on behalf of the public
Governed by the statute creating it

learn.title: Comparing the forms of business organization

blocks.text: Examiners frequently ask for a comparison, and the safest structure is to take one basis at a time across all the forms. On formation, a sole proprietorship needs no legal formality while a company requires registration under the Companies Act. On liability, it is unlimited for the proprietor and general partners, and limited to the amount invested for company shareholders. On continuity, the proprietorship ends with the owner, the partnership dissolves on a partner’s exit unless the agreement says otherwise, and a company continues regardless of who holds shares.

blocks.caption: Comparison of the forms of business organisation
rows: Registration as a society or co-op
Created by statute or executive decision
Service to members at fair terms

blocks.text: No form is best in general, and the choice must follow from the circumstances of the particular venture. The factors that decide it are the amount of capital required and how many people can be persuaded to supply it, the extent to which the owners are willing to expose personal assets to the debts of the business, the need for the firm to continue beyond the lifetime or withdrawal of any one owner, and the degree of regulation, disclosure and formal compliance the business can afford to carry. A firm that answers these four questions honestly will usually find that only one or two of the forms remain seriously available.

Partnership: each partner personally liable without limit
Company: claim stops at the amount unpaid on shares
Cooperative: liability limited to the member’s contribution

figures.caption: Figure: Choosing a form by capital and continuity need
figures.description: A decision path starting at a box for how much capital is needed, branching to small capital leading to sole proprietorship, moderate capital leading to partnership or cooperative, and large capital leading to the company, with a side branch for strategic necessity leading to a public-sector undertaking.

Small capital from one person: sole proprietorship
Moderate capital from a few: partnership or cooperative
Large capital from many: company form
Strategic or public necessity: public-sector undertaking

keyPoints: A sole proprietorship has unlimited liability but the simplest formation and full control.
Partnership rests on mutual agency: each partner can bind the firm in ordinary business.
In an ordinary partnership every partner is jointly and severally liable without limit.
A limited liability partnership caps the liability of ordinary partners at their contribution.
A company is an artificial person with perpetual succession and limited liability for shareholders.
A private limited company cannot invite the public for capital and restricts share transfer.
A public limited company needs seven members and may be listed, with full disclosure duties.
A cooperative works on one member one vote for the common benefit of its members.
A public-sector undertaking serves public interest and is controlled by the government.
The choice of form depends on capital, liability, continuity and the regulation the business can bear.
examFocus: This unit carries 25 marks, so comparison questions expect all forms against one basis rather than one form in isolation.
Merits and limitations questions are marked in pairs, so give the strength and its matching weakness.
In company questions, quote the minimum membership difference between a private and a public limited company.

vocabulary.meaning: Business owned and managed by one person with unlimited liability.
Each partner can bind the firm through acts done in the ordinary course of business.
Owners’ personal assets are reachable for the debts of the business.
Owners lose at most the amount they have invested or guaranteed.
The organisation continues regardless of changes in its ownership.
Voluntary association of persons with limited means for a common economic purpose.
Enterprise owned or controlled by the government to serve public interest.

questions.prompt: The greatest limitation of a sole proprietorship is:
options: Unlimited personal liability and limited capital
questions.answer: Unlimited personal liability and limited capital
questions.explanation: The owner is personally liable for every business debt and the capital is confined to what she can raise herself, which together cap the size of the venture.

questions.prompt: In a partnership, mutual agency means:
options: Every partner is liable only for her own acts
Each partner can bind the firm in the ordinary course of business
questions.answer: Each partner can bind the firm in the ordinary course of business
questions.explanation: Acts done in the ordinary course of business by one partner bind all the partners, which is what makes partnership a relation of agency.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly states the minimum membership of a private and a public limited company?
questions.explanation: A private limited company needs two members while a public limited company needs seven before it can commence business.

questions.prompt: A firm that buys in bulk and sells to members at fair prices, with each member holding one vote, is a:
questions.explanation: Bulk purchase for member benefit on the principle of one member one vote defines a consumer cooperative.

questions.prompt: A partner who contributes capital but takes no part in management is called a __________ partner.
questions.explanation: A dormant or sleeping partner contributes capital and shares profit without participating in day-to-day decisions.

questions.prompt: The feature of a company by which it continues to exist irrespective of changes in its membership is called __________ succession.
questions.explanation: Because the company is a separate legal person, the departure or death of shareholders does not affect its existence.

questions.prompt: State four merits of the sole proprietorship form.
questions.answer: Four merits are: the decision of the owner is taken quickly without consultation; the capital required to start is small; the owner retains full control and the entire profit as direct incentive; and formation is simple with little legal compliance. Personal contact with customers is also accepted.
questions.explanation: Each merit must be tied to a feature of the form, since listing without linking earns only partial credit.

questions.prompt: What is a limited liability partnership and why was it introduced?
questions.answer: A limited liability partnership is a form in which at least two designated partners hold unlimited liability while the liability of every other partner is limited to the amount she has contributed. It was introduced because in an ordinary partnership each partner is jointly and severally liable without limit, so one partner’s negligence could destroy another’s personal wealth, and because an ordinary partnership leaves a partner exposed to the unauthorised acts of the others.
questions.explanation: The answer needs the mechanism of designated partners and the specific weakness it corrects.

questions.prompt: Compare a partnership and a company on formation, liability, continuity and management.
questions.answer: On formation, a partnership arises from an agreement between persons to share profits, with registration optional but without it the firm cannot sue to enforce its contracts, while a company must be incorporated under the Companies Act and receives a certificate of incorporation before it can act. On liability, partners in an ordinary partnership are jointly and severally liable without limit, whereas a shareholder’s liability is limited to the amount unpaid on her shares. On continuity, a partnership is disturbed by the retirement or death of a partner unless the agreement provides otherwise, while a company enjoys perpetual succession and continues irrespective of changes in ownership. On management, partners manage the firm themselves under mutual agency, while a company is managed by a board of directors elected by the shareholders, who may in turn appoint professional managers.
questions.explanation: All four bases must be compared rather than described separately, because the comparison itself carries the marks.

questions.prompt: Two brothers run a furniture workshop with their own savings and a bank overdraft. They have just secured a large export order that needs four times their current capital and hiring a production manager. Recommend a form of organisation and justify it on four bases.
questions.answer: The order changes the requirements of the business: capital far beyond what two individuals can contribute personally, and management that cannot be supervised personally while the brothers deal with the export customer. A private limited company is the most suitable form, since it allows capital to be raised from investors while restricting the transfer of shares and keeping the firm under family control, and it forbids a public invitation that would dilute that control. On liability, the brothers’ personal assets are protected, which matters because an export order carries compensation risk in the contract. On continuity, the company continues regardless of their availability, which reassures the overseas buyer who needs a stable counterparty. On management, the production manager can be appointed with defined authority within the board structure. A partnership would be cheaper to form, but unlimited liability and difficulty of raising the required capital make it unsuitable, while a cooperative or public-sector undertaking does not fit a private export business at all.
questions.explanation: Full marks require selecting one form and then justifying it on at least four bases, including why the obvious alternatives were rejected.
